body:
I tried to reproduce this in Godot 4.6.2...

First of all, as far as I can tell we are not talking about the inspector (a csgbox3d does not show in the inspector, nor is there a way to zoom in the inspector preview of meshes). Thus, I assume we are talking about the 3D workspace.

I think what is happening is that the view is lined up back to the same exact orientation after "looking around".

It is important to recognize that the "zoom out" (mouse wheel down) is not technically a "zoom", but a dolly (and this is standard in 3D applications, and what users have come to expect). So when we zoom out, the camera is moving backwards. In the case of Godot this goes to 1000.0m (as shown in the bottom of the blue bar), and Godot remembers this distance, to which I'll refer to as "zoom value".

After you "zoomed out" you look around, which I interpret as you holding the secondary click and moving the mouse so the camera rotates in place, and then "zoom in" (mouse wheel up)… which moves the camera forth, the 1000.0m or whatever zoom value that you "zoomed out" as it decrements it. Since the camera is moving forth, a small angle misalignment is amplified (1 degree off course after 1km takes you 17.45m off of your destination, the formula is distance * sin(angle)). As a result, you end away from the csgbox3d you were looking, and since it is away, it looks smaller than it did before "zooming out".

A quick fix for this situation is to select the csgbox3d and pressing F, this should center it into view (this moves the camera to where the selected 3D node is, it does not change the zoom value).

If I'm correct on my interpretation, the perception that this is a bug should go away by having an scenario. When the csgbox3d is the only thing in the world, you don't have something else for reference (except the axis lines), making it easier to think that the csgbox3d somehow became smaller instead of the camera being in a different position.

If I'm mistaken on my interpretation, please provide more detailed/corrected instructions to reproduce.
